terms.meaning: a way of reading a file piece by piece instead of all at once

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Size limits for text and tables
sections.what: Sets the largest allowed single text line at 16 million characters and the widest allowed table at 2,048 columns.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops one malformed file from consuming all memory.
sections.watch_out: Raising these limits increases memory use for every reader that uses them.

sections.name: bounded_text_lines
sections.title: Reading text lines safely
sections.what: Reads a text file one line at a time, but refuses any line over the limit by skipping its remainder and raising a clear error.
sections.why: Stops a file with no line breaks from being loaded into memory in one piece.
sections.watch_out: The error stops the whole ingestion, so one oversized line rejects the entire file.

summary: Sets the size limits that protect the app from oversized text lines and very wide tables.
purpose: Stops one malformed or hostile file from using up all the memory.
why: Likely reason: text files with no line breaks, or tables with thousands of columns, could otherwise be loaded whole.
how: Two fixed limits are defined. A line reader asks for a line in capped pieces, and if a line is longer than the limit it skips the rest of that line and raises a clear error.
inputs: An open text stream and an optional character limit.
outputs: One line at a time, or an error naming the limit.
risks: One oversized line fails the entire ingestion. Raising the limits increases memory use for every reader that relies on them.
debug: If a file is rejected with a record size error, check whether the file has very long lines or missing line breaks. The limits are set at the top of the file.
